tracks.title: Requiem in C minor: Introitus et Kyrie
tracks.fact: Beethoven considered Cherubini the greatest living composer of his time, and this Requiem was performed at Beethoven's funeral in 1827.

tracks.title: Médée (Medea): Overture
tracks.fact: Brahms admired the overture to Medea immensely, keeping it as a permanent reference score in his study.

tracks.title: Symphony in D major: I. Largo - Allegro molto
tracks.fact: Cherubini's only symphony was commissioned directly by the Royal Philharmonic Society in London in 1815.

tracks.title: Marche funèbre
tracks.fact: Composed in 1820 following the assassination of the Duke of Berry, noted for its unusually stark instrumentation.

tracks.title: String Quartet No. 1 in E-flat major
tracks.fact: Cherubini began writing string quartets only after turning fifty, directly modeling them on Haydn's late works.

tracks.title: Ave Maria
tracks.fact: An intimate sacred piece written for soprano and English horn during his service at the Royal Chapel in Paris.

tracks.title: The Planets, Op. 32: Mars, the Bringer of War
tracks.fact: Holst's relentless ostinato rhythm in Mars heavily influenced generations of film score composers, including John Williams in Star Wars.

tracks.title: The Planets, Op. 32: Jupiter, the Bringer of Jollity
tracks.fact: The central noble melody of Jupiter was later adapted into the patriotic British hymn 'I Vow to Thee, My Country'.

tracks.title: The Planets, Op. 32: Venus, the Bringer of Peace
tracks.fact: Venus offers a serene contrast to Mars, opening with gentle horn calls and peaceful string textures.

tracks.title: St Paul's Suite, Op. 29, No. 2: Jig
tracks.fact: Written for the string orchestra of St Paul's Girls' School where Holst served as Director of Music.

tracks.title: Brook Green Suite: III. Dance
tracks.fact: A delightful late work designed specifically for developing student musicians to perform with professional quality.

tracks.title: The Planets, Op. 32: Neptune, the Mystic
tracks.fact: Features a pioneering use of an off-stage female chorus that fades away into total silence without a final cadence.

tracks.title: Rhapsody in Blue
tracks.fact: Premiered in 1924 during a concert titled 'An Experiment in Modern Music', establishing Gershwin's fame overnight.

tracks.title: An American in Paris
tracks.fact: Gershwin actually integrated real Parisian taxi horns that he purchased in France directly into the orchestral score.

tracks.title: Porgy and Bess: Summertime
tracks.fact: One of the most covered songs in recorded music history, drawing deeply from African-American spiritual and blues traditions.

tracks.title: Cuban Overture
tracks.fact: Inspired by a two-week vacation in Havana, Cuba, utilizing native percussion instruments like maracas and bongos.

tracks.title: Three Preludes: I. Allegro ben ritmato e deciso
tracks.fact: Originally conceived as part of a larger collection of twenty-four preludes for solo piano.

tracks.title: Porgy and Bess: I Got Plenty o' Nuttin'
tracks.fact: An exuberant folk tune reflecting joyful resilience in Catfish Row.

tracks.title: The Carnival of the Animals: The Swan
tracks.fact: Saint-Saëns prohibited the full performance of his humorous suite during his lifetime, fearing it would damage his serious reputation.

tracks.title: Danse Macabre, Op. 40
tracks.fact: Features the xylophone to imitate rattling skeleton bones and an eerie solo violin tuning down a tritone.

tracks.title: Symphony No. 3 in C minor 'Organ': II. Maestoso
tracks.fact: Dedicated to the memory of Franz Liszt; uses a massive pipe organ and piano four-hands.

tracks.title: Introduction and Rondo Capriccioso, Op. 28
tracks.fact: Composed specifically for the legendary Spanish violin virtuoso Pablo de Sarasate.

tracks.title: Cello Concerto No. 1 in A minor: I. Allegro non troppo
tracks.fact: Renowned for its continuous form where all three movements flow directly into one another without pauses.

tracks.title: The Carnival of the Animals: Aquarium
tracks.fact: Utilizes shimmering glass harmonica/celesta textures to create an enchanting underwater atmosphere.

tracks.title: Nabucco: Va, pensiero (Chorus of the Hebrew Slaves)
tracks.fact: Became an unofficial national anthem for Italy during the Risorgimento unification movement.

tracks.title: Requiem: Dies irae
tracks.fact: Famed for its explosive, thunderous bass drum strikes and terrifying choral outbursts.

tracks.title: La traviata: Brindisi (Libiamo ne' lieti calici)
tracks.fact: One of the most famous drinking songs in opera history, sparkling with celebratory charm.

tracks.title: Rigoletto: La donna è mobile
tracks.fact: Verdi kept the melody secret prior to the premiere, forbidding the tenor to whistle it outside rehearsals.

tracks.title: Aida: Grand March (Triumphal March)
tracks.fact: Requires specialized long Egyptian trumpets constructed specifically for the opera's grand spectacle.

tracks.title: Il trovatore: Anvil Chorus (Vedi! Le fosche notturne spoglie)
tracks.fact: Features actual blacksmith hammers striking anvils in rhythm with the joyful gypsy chorus.

tracks.title: Hungarian Rhapsody No. 2 in C-sharp minor
tracks.fact: Widely popularized in classic animation cartoons, setting a benchmark for supreme piano virtuosity.

tracks.title: Liebestraum No. 3 in A-flat major
tracks.fact: Originally written as a song setting for tenor poetry before being adapted into a beloved solo piano nocturne.

tracks.title: La Campanella
tracks.fact: Based on Paganini's violin concerto, demanding extreme hand leaps and lightning-fast precision.

tracks.title: Consolation No. 3 in D-flat major
tracks.fact: A tender, meditative miniature offering tranquil emotional sanctuary.

tracks.title: Totentanz (Dance of Death)
tracks.fact: Built entirely around variations of the medieval 'Dies Irae' plainchant melody.

tracks.title: Les Préludes, S.97
tracks.fact: One of the earliest symphonic poems, establishing a brand-new orchestral genre for the Romantic era.

tracks.title: Prince Igor: Polovtsian Dances
tracks.fact: Borodin was a professional professor of chemistry by day and composed classical masterpieces only in his spare time.

tracks.title: In the Steppes of Central Asia
tracks.fact: Depicts a peaceful caravan journey across the Asian desert accompanied by Russian and Oriental melodies.

tracks.title: String Quartet No. 2 in D major: III. Notturno (Andante)
tracks.fact: Borodin dedicated this gorgeous movement as a romantic anniversary gift to his wife.

tracks.title: Symphony No. 2 in B minor: I. Allegro
tracks.fact: Described as a 'heroic epic' capturing the spirit of ancient Russian knights and warriors.

tracks.title: Symphony No. 1 in E-flat major: III. Scherzo
tracks.fact: Written under the direct mentorship and encouragement of Mily Balakirev.

tracks.title: Petite Suite: No. 1, Au couvent
tracks.fact: A charming piano suite later orchestrated by Alexander Glazunov.

tracks.title: Finlandia, Op. 26
tracks.fact: Became an iconic symbol of Finnish national resistance against Russian imperial censorship.

tracks.title: Violin Concerto in D minor: I. Allegro moderato
tracks.fact: Sibelius originally aspired to become a professional concert violinist before turning full-time to composition.

tracks.title: Valse Triste, Op. 44, No. 1
tracks.fact: A hauntingly melancholic waltz written as incidental music for a play about a dying mother dancing with ghosts.

tracks.title: Karelia Suite: III. Alla marcia
tracks.fact: Commissioned to raise funds for a student association in Vyborg.

tracks.title: The Swan of Tuonela, Op. 22, No. 2
tracks.fact: Features a prominent English horn solo portraying a majestic swan gliding on the dark waters of the underworld.

tracks.title: Symphony No. 2 in D major: IV. Finale
tracks.fact: Capped by a triumphant trumpet motif that embodies national awakening and liberation.

tracks.title: Symphonie fantastique: IV. March to the Scaffold
tracks.fact: Berlioz composed this hallucinatory masterpiece inspired by his obsessive unrequited love for actress Harriet Smithson.

tracks.title: Symphonie fantastique: V. Dream of a Witches' Sabbath
tracks.fact: Parodies the sacred 'Dies Irae' chant amidst demonic sorcery and howling witches.

tracks.title: Roman Carnival Overture, Op. 9
tracks.fact: Incorporates thematic material from Berlioz's early, unsuccessful opera Benvenuto Cellini.

tracks.title: Requiem (Grande messe des morts): Agnus Dei
tracks.fact: Calls for colossal musical forces, including four separate brass choirs positioned at the corners of the orchestra.

tracks.title: The Damnation of Faust: Rákóczi March
tracks.fact: Arranged specifically so that Berlioz could perform it during his triumphant concert tours across Hungary.

tracks.title: L'enfance du Christ: The Shepherds' Farewell
tracks.fact: Originally published anonymously under a fabricated 17th-century composer name to trick conservative critics.

tracks.title: Symphony No. 9 in D minor, Op. 125: IV. Ode to Joy
tracks.fact: Beethoven was completely deaf by the time this choral masterpiece premiered, yet he turned to accept the roaring applause.

tracks.title: Symphony No. 5 in C minor, Op. 67: I. Allegro con brio
tracks.fact: The iconic opening four-note motif is famously interpreted as 'fate knocking at the door'.

tracks.title: Piano Sonata No. 14 in C-sharp minor 'Moonlight': I. Adagio sostenuto
tracks.fact: The nickname 'Moonlight' was attached by a music critic years after Beethoven's death, inspired by Lake Lucerne.

tracks.title: Bagatelle No. 25 in A minor 'Für Elise'
tracks.fact: The original manuscript was lost for decades and only published 40 years after Beethoven's death.

tracks.title: Piano Concerto No. 5 in E-flat major 'Emperor': I. Allegro
tracks.fact: Beethoven's final piano concerto, monumental in scale and overflowing with regal heroism.

tracks.title: Coriolan Overture, Op. 62
tracks.fact: Portrays the dramatic psychological conflict of a Roman general torn between vengeance and mercy.

event_note: Christmas Eve – Exquisite Baroque and Classical Christmas Masterpieces

tracks.title: Concerto Grosso in G minor, Op. 6, No. 8 'Fatto per la notte di Natale'
tracks.fact: Corelli's famous 'Christmas Concerto' was composed specifically for Christmas Eve performance and features a subtle pastoral final movement.

tracks.title: The Nutcracker: Dance of the Sugar Plum Fairy
tracks.fact: Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky was among the first to use the newly imported celesta instrument from Paris in this piece.

tracks.title: The Nutcracker: Waltz of the Flowers
tracks.fact: This grand waltz from The Nutcracker remains one of the most widely recognized orchestral ballet pieces in the world.

tracks.title: Pastorale in F major
tracks.fact: A traditional Italian Christmas melody frequently adapted by Baroque masters for holiday celebrations.

tracks.title: Hodie Christus natus est (Jan Pieterszoon Sweelinck)
tracks.fact: A luminous Renaissance Christmas motet rich in intricate vocal polyphony.

tracks.title: Silent Night (Choral Version)
tracks.fact: The world's most popular carol, composed in 1818 in Austria by Franz Xaver Gruber.

event_note: Christmas Day – Monumental Baroque Sacred Masterpieces

tracks.title: Christmas Oratorio, BWV 248: Part I - Jauchzet, frohlocket
tracks.fact: The opening part of Bach's Christmas Oratorio bursts forth with powerful timpani strokes and triumphant trumpets celebrating the Nativity.

tracks.title: Christmas Oratorio, BWV 248: Pastoral Symphony (Sinfonia)
tracks.fact: An instrumental interlude introducing Part II, depicting the peaceful Bethlehem night and the watching shepherds.

tracks.title: Magnificat in D major, BWV 243: I. Magnificat anima mea
tracks.fact: Bach originally composed this brilliant setting for the Christmas vespers service in Leipzig in 1723.

tracks.title: Wachet auf, ruft uns die Stimme, BWV 140
tracks.fact: One of Bach's most celebrated chorale cantatas, blending deep spiritual devotion with majestic counterpoint.

tracks.title: Orchestral Suite No. 3 in D major: Air on the G String
tracks.fact: A piece of profound tranquility, offering an ideal soundtrack for a peaceful holiday morning.

tracks.title: Jesu, Joy of Man's Desiring
tracks.fact: Bach's iconic chorale setting brings deep inner peace and has become a permanent staple of classical holiday playlists.

event_note: Boxing Day – Monumental Choral and Orchestral Masterpieces

tracks.title: Messiah, HWV 56: Hallelujah Chorus
tracks.fact: King George II was so moved by the power of this chorus that he stood up, inspiring the enduring tradition of audience standing.

tracks.title: Messiah, HWV 56: For Unto Us a Child Is Born
tracks.fact: A joyous chorus from Messiah adapted from an Italian secular duet into a monumental sacred masterpiece.

tracks.title: Water Music: Suite in F major, HWV 348: Allegro
tracks.fact: First performed on a barge on the River Thames for the British monarch, exuding festive brilliance and courtly elegance.

tracks.title: Music for the Royal Fireworks: La Rejouissance
tracks.fact: Commissioned by the King for the public celebration of the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle, featuring an imposing wind band.

tracks.title: Messiah, HWV 56: Pastoral Symphony
tracks.fact: Another exquisite pastoral movement within our holiday collection, setting a contemplative and atmospheric mood.

tracks.title: Zadok the Priest (Coronation Anthem)
tracks.fact: Handel composed this anthem for the coronation of George II in 1727; it has since been performed at every British coronation.
